root_cause.text: The ath12k WoW/offload code iterated over all per-link `arvif` entries in an MLO connection and applied wake/offload setup to secondary links as well as the primary `deflink`, causing WCN7850 firmware to crash because the firmware only supports these WoW offloads on the primary link.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (arvif != &arvif->ahvif->deflink) continue;` in multiple WoW/offload paths (`ath12k_wow_cleanup()`, `ath12k_wow_set_wakeups()`, `ath12k_wow_nlo_cleanup()`, `ath12k_wow_arp_ns_offload()`, `ath12k_gtk_rekey_offload()`), and the commit message explicitly states: “In case of multi-link connection, WCN7850 firmware crashes due to WoW offloads enabled on both primary and secondary links. Change to do it only on primary link to fix it.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict WOW cleanup to default vif links to avoid cleaning up non-default link entries.
intent_record.what: In ath12k_wow_cleanup(), a new conditional check was added inside the arvif iteration: if the current arvif is not equal to its ahvif->deflink, the loop now skips cleanup for that entry and continues to the next one.
intent_record.how: At runtime, WOW cleanup is now performed only for the default link of each vif instead of for every link object in the ar->arvifs list. This prevents non-default link instances from being passed to ath12k_wow_vif_cleanup(), avoiding redundant or incorrect cleanup work.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict WOW wakeup configuration to each vif's default link to avoid applying it to non-default links.
intent_record.what: Inside ath12k_wow_set_wakeups(), the loop over ar->arvifs gained a new conditional that skips any arvif that is not the ahvif's deflink, before the existing P2P vdev check and wakeup configuration call.
intent_record.how: At runtime, wakeup settings will now only be applied to the default link of each vif, preventing the function from attempting to configure wakeups on non-default links and avoiding duplicate or incorrect per-link setup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict WOW NLO cleanup to default-link vif entries to avoid processing non-default links.
intent_record.what: In ath12k_wow_nlo_cleanup(), two lines were added inside the ar->arvifs list iteration: a check that skips the loop body unless the current arvif pointer equals &arvif->ahvif->deflink, followed by a continue statement.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the cleanup logic will now only operate on the default link vdev for each vif and ignore any non-default link entries in the arvifs list. This prevents the function from processing additional link instances that should not be included in WOW NLO cleanup, avoiding unintended cleanup work on non-default links.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict WoW ARP/NS offload handling to default-link STA interfaces only.
intent_record.what: Inside ath12k_wow_arp_ns_offload(), a new check was added in the arvif iteration: if the current arvif is not equal to ahvif->deflink, the loop now continues and skips that entry before the existing vdev type STA check.
intent_record.how: At runtime, ARP/NS WoW offload handling is now restricted to the default link of each multi-link virtual interface, preventing non-default link vif instances from being processed by this code path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Limit GTK rekey offload handling to default-link arvifs to avoid acting on non-default links.
intent_record.what: Inside ath12k_gtk_rekey_offload(), a new early-continue check was added at the start of the arvif iteration: if the current arvif is not equal to arvif->ahvif->deflink, the loop skips to the next entry.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now ignores non-default-link virtual interfaces when processing GTK rekey offload, so only the default link for each vif is considered for enabling or disabling offload.

Restrict wireless offload handling to default-link interfaces so rekey/ARP/NS processing only applies to the primary link.

relevance_review.reason: The changes explicitly limit WoW/offload handling to the default link, which directly matches the root cause: the code was wrongly iterating over all per-link arvif entries and applying WoW setup/cleanup to secondary links, causing firmware crashes.

The changes explicitly restrict WoW/offload processing to the default-link interface and prevent ARP/NS and GTK rekey offloads from being applied to secondary MLO links, which matches the root cause of the firmware crash caused by handling offloads on non-primary links.

candidates.rationale: This loop walks all per-link arvif entries, which is the root cause: WoW cleanup is applied to secondary MLO links as well as the primary deflink instead of being restricted to the default link.
This loop iterates over every link-specific arvif in the vif, causing wakeup setup to be applied to non-default links that the firmware does not support for WoW offloads.
This loop processes all arvif entries during NLO cleanup, so non-default MLO links are handled too, matching the bug pattern of applying WoW-related handling beyond the primary link.
This loop iterates over all STA arvifs, including secondary links, which is the vulnerable behavior for ARP/NS offload because the firmware only supports these offloads on the primary link.
This loop walks all STA arvifs and therefore includes non-default links in GTK rekey offload handling, which can trigger firmware crashes when offload is applied outside the primary link.

vuln_statements.explanation: This loop iterates over every per-link arvif in an MLO vif, so WoW/offload setup and cleanup were applied to secondary links as well as the primary deflink. That matches the root cause: WCN7850 firmware only supports these WoW offloads on the primary link, and processing all links can crash the firmware.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet clearly shows WoW wakeup/offload setup being applied to every vif in the device, not just the primary link. In `ath12k_wow_cleanup()` and `ath12k_wow_set_wakeups()` the code uses `list_for_each_entry(arvif, &ar->arvifs, list)` and then calls per-vdev WoW operations for each entry: `ath12k_wmi_wow_add_wakeup_event(... arvif->vdev_id, ...)`, `ath12k_wmi_wow_del_pattern(... arvif->vdev_id, ...)`, and `ath12k_wmi_wow_add_pattern(... arvif->vdev_id, ...)`. There is no check for `deflink` or primary-link-only handling anywhere in `ath12k_vif_wow_set_wakeups()`, `ath12k_wow_set_wakeups()`, or `ath12k_wow_cleanup()`. Since the root cause is that MLO secondary links were incorrectly included and WCN7850 firmware only supports these WoW offloads on the primary link, this code contains the vulnerable construct and does not yet contain the fix.
